description: CSUTLDTC, the called date-validation subprogram, exercised as the @Service it became (util.DateUtilityJob) and never through a JobLauncher or an HTTP layer: no EXEC PGM= anywhere in app/jcl or app/proc names it, and it is CALLed four times from two online programs - CORPT00C at L392 and L412, COTRN02C at L393 and L413. LS-DATE='2022-07-19' and LS-DATE-FORMAT='YYYY-MM-DD' are this case's two LINKAGE SECTION parameters (L84-L85), each written out to the declared PIC X(10) width; LS-RESULT PIC X(80) (L86) is the entire output and is asserted below as the single WS_MESSAGE_80 line. That mask is the one both real callers pass - WS-DATE-FORMAT PIC X(10) VALUE 'YYYY-MM-DD' at CORPT00C L72 and COTRN02C L60, moved into CSUTLDTC-DATE-FORMAT immediately before each CALL - and both callers treat severity '0000' as accepted (CORPT00C L396, COTRN02C L397). The program declares no SELECT and opens no file, so it seeds no dataset, writes no record and takes no job parameter; its whole observable behaviour is the 80 bytes L97 moves into LS-RESULT and the severity L98 moves into RETURN-CODE. This case pins arm 1 of the EVALUATE TRUE at L128-L149: FC-INVALID-DATE, whose 88-level VALUE is X'0000000000000000' (L62). Despite its name that all-zeros token is the SUCCESS token - the SEVERITY and MSG-NO halfwords declared at L72-L73 inside CASE-1-CONDITION-ID both decode to zero, so the numeric REDEFINES views WS-SEVERITY-N (L44) and WS-MSG-NO-N (L47) written at L123 and L124 render '0000' and '0000' zero-filled to four digits, RETURN-CODE is 0, and the arm moves 'Date is valid' into WS-RESULT PIC X(15) (L130), right space-padded to fifteen. The inverted condition name is preserved, not corrected. WS-DATE at offset 45 is deliberately NOT the date: L105-L106 moves LENGTH OF LS-DATE - the declared length, hence always 10 - into VSTRING-LENGTH, and L122 then moves the whole WS-DATE-TO-TEST group into WS-DATE PIC X(10), so the two-byte binary halfword X'000A' survives and only the first eight text bytes '2022-07-' follow it, the trailing '9' being truncated on the right. That corruption is expected output and is likewise preserved. WS-DATE-FMT at offset 66 is by contrast clean, because L111-L113 set it by an ordinary X(10) to X(10) move before the CALL and L122 targets WS-DATE alone. Expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED by structured reading of app/cbl/CSUTLDTC.cbl - the 01 WS-MESSAGE declaration at L42-L57 summed span by span to exactly 80 bytes, the nine feedback tokens at L62-L70, the group move at L122 and the EVALUATE at L128-L149 - and were NOT captured from any execution of the COBOL, which is impossible in this environment: PROCEDURE DIVISION USING at L88 makes this a subprogram the available compiler refuses to build as an executable, and no Language Environment services are reachable, so the CALL "CEEDAYS" at L116 that decides every outcome has no implementation to call. Only the provenance of the expectation is substituted; the twenty-case set, the field-by-field diff and the diff-count-of-zero gate all stand.
